evals.name: sse-hub-and-browser-auth
evals.prompt: Our Arc for Elixir app serves an observable query to a React app that must not use WebSockets. How do we use the SSE hub, how does the browser authenticate it, and what happens to the control POSTs?
evals.expected_output: Use the multiplexed SSE hub (QueryTransportMethod.ServerSentEvents). A browser EventSource cannot set headers so use cookies read by a plug or handler. Control POSTs must come from the caller that opened the stream.
assertions: Selects the shared SSE hub at /.cratis/queries/sse with subscribe and unsubscribe POST routes, and the client QueryTransportMethod.ServerSentEvents, not a per-query direct stream.
States a browser EventSource and WebSocket cannot set request headers, so authentication uses cookies read by a plug or authentication handler.
States a control request from an unknown connection or a different caller than the one that opened the stream is answered 404, and a malformed body 400.
Does not recommend trust_forwarded_identity_headers: true as a production authentication scheme; it trusts unsigned headers from any caller and is for samples or an ingress that sets them.

evals.name: tenant-selection-is-not-membership
evals.prompt: We set tenancy: [resolver: :header] in Arc for Elixir and the MongoDB database follows the tenant. Is a customer safe from reading another tenant's data now?
evals.expected_output: No. A resolver only selects; membership must be checked. A named tenant selects database<database>+<tenant> and the Chronicle namespace; use the :claim resolver or an Arc.Filter or policy to authorize membership.
assertions: States a resolver only selects the tenant, because the header is chosen by the caller, and that Arc does not check membership.
Tells the user to authorize tenant membership themselves, for example with the :claim resolver, a policy or an Arc.Filter.
Explains a named tenant uses the database database+tenant and the Chronicle namespace, and that nil, an empty value and Default are the default tenant.
Does not invent a chain of tenant resolvers; Arc for Elixir configures one resolver.

evals.name: mongodb-observation-needs-a-replica-set
evals.prompt: Our observable Arc.MongoDB query never updates in a docker standalone mongo. We use watch: [Arc.MongoDB.watch(Book)]. Why, and what else must be in the supervision tree?
evals.expected_output: Change streams require a replica set or sharded cluster; a single node with --replSet is enough. Arc.MongoDB must be started after the Arc application in the supervision tree.
assertions: Explains change streams need a replica set or sharded cluster, and that a single node started with --replSet and initiated is enough.
Shows {Arc.MongoDB, application: MyApp.Arc} in the supervision tree after the Arc application.
Mentions one shared database-level change stream per database, which resumes from its token.

evals.name: colocated-vertical-slices
evals.prompt: We want the Elixir, generated TypeScript proxy and React page of each Arc for Elixir feature in one folder. How do we configure it and what must the JS tooling do?
evals.expected_output: Use arc: [application:, output: "lib", layout: :colocated]; put package.json and node_modules above lib; include lib in tsconfig and the bundler; commit generated files and use --check in CI.
assertions: Configures the :arc compiler with layout: :colocated and an output that is the root holding both Elixir and React code, such as lib.
States package.json and node_modules must sit above lib so each slice resolves @cratis/arc, and the TypeScript and bundler configuration must include lib.
States generated files carry an @generated marker, a file without it is never overwritten, and recommends committing them with mix arc.gen.proxies --check in CI.
Keeps shared concepts out of a slice and has slices reach each other only through commands, queries or shared contracts.
